Definition: Is the register integrated with the government's national data exchange system?
Comments: No interoperability with national data exchange; no data sharing agreements.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the cited World Bank Equatorial Guinea Digital Economy Diagnostic (2023). It explicitly states that a 'currently absent national interoperability framework' hampers integration across ministries, with agencies including the civil registry (SIREC) building systems in silos. Cross-checked with Biometric Update's July 2024 summary of the same report, and searched for later developments (2025 CRVS regional meeting hosted in Malabo, INEGE census planning) which show continued modernisation efforts but no evidence of a national data exchange platform having since been established. Score of 1=No confirmed.
revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea's civil registry system, SIREC (Sistema Informático del Registro Civil), operates outside any national government data exchange platform. The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic for Equatorial Guinea finds that no national interoperability framework exists, with government ministries, including civil registration, developing digital systems independently rather than through a shared exchange infrastructure.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the national ID system?
Comments: Civil registry has no interoperability with national ID system.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the cited World Bank report, which states the country lacks a foundational digital identification system and operational trust framework for digital authentication, and recommends 'implementing a digital identity ecosystem' as a priority reform. No national digital ID system exists for the civil registry to link to. Biometric Update's 2024 coverage of the same report confirms this remains an outstanding recommendation. No subsequent evidence found of a digital ID system having launched. Score of 1=No confirmed.
revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea has not established a national digital identity system, so its civil registry (SIREC) has no digital ID database with which to integrate. The World Bank's Digital Economy Diagnostic identifies the absence of a foundational identification system and a digital authentication trust framework as a core gap, recommending that the government first build this infrastructure before civil registration data can be linked to a national ID.

Definition: Is the register integrated with the population register?
Comments: No integration with population register; no population register exists.
revision_notes: Fetched and read the cited World Bank report, which confirms a fragmented digital public platform landscape with no interoperability framework. Checked the national statistics office (INEGE) directly: Equatorial Guinea's demographic data comes from periodic decennial-style censuses (1983, 1994, 2001, 2015, with the fifth due in 2025), not a continuously updated population register, corroborating the claim that no such register exists for the civil registry to integrate with. Score of 1=No confirmed.
revised_comments: Equatorial Guinea does not maintain a continuously updated national population register; demographic data instead derives from periodic population and housing censuses conducted by INEGE (most recently 2015, with a fifth census planned). As no population register exists, the civil registration system (SIREC) has no such register to integrate with.
